title: ～なさい — “do ～” (gentle command)
summary: ～なさい is a command used by someone in a position of authority, such as a parent, teacher or the instructions on a test paper. It attaches to the ます-stem and is softer than a bare imperative, but it is still an order and not for superiors.

patterns.form: 動詞ます形の語幹 ＋ なさい
patterns.gloss: 寝る → 寝なさい / 食べる → 食べなさい / 洗う → 洗いなさい

patterns.form: お／ご ＋ 名詞（する動詞）＋ なさい
patterns.gloss: Formal usage in instructions: 次の文を読みなさい

body.p: It is the imperative なさい of the honorific verb なさる, attached to another verb. It once meant a polite “please do ～,” but today it is an instruction used by parents to children and by teachers to students.
Use it for instructions at home and school: もう遅いから、早く寝なさい, 野菜もちゃんと食べなさい, 手を洗ってから食事をしなさい. Test questions use 選びなさい and 答えなさい.
It is softer than the plain imperative (食べろ), but still an order. To friends, use ～て or ～よう; to superiors, use ～てください or ～てくださいませんか.

examples.ja: もう遅（おそ）いから、早（はや）く寝（ね）なさい。
examples.tr: It's late, so go to bed early.

examples.ja: 野菜（やさい）もちゃんと食（た）べなさい。
手（て）を洗（あら）ってから食事（しょくじ）をしなさい。
examples.romaji: Te o aratte kara shokuji o shinasai.
examples.tr: Wash your hands before you eat.

pitfalls: Never use it to superiors. 先生、見なさい is rude; say ご覧ください.
Attach it to the ます-stem. 食べるなさい and 食べてなさい are wrong.
